Evidence: 23 durable sources from Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, CanadaBuys, corporate and IP registries, ANVIL and Canadian Army Today support the proposed leaves. reviewWarnings: No reviewed source establishes whether ANVIL Platform, Smithy, Offline Speech Translation and Vulcan are modules, releases or separate products.

Vulcan is Available for testing, which is a pre-test status and not a match, contract, completed evaluation, performance result or adoption.
The three disclosed defence contracts do not identify a current product, named end user, completed test result or operational deployment.
The SLSA and SBIPS instruments show CAD 0 and support supplier eligibility only, not revenue, buyer demand, call-ups or customer use.
Federal lobbying records prove contract pursuit and communication, not government interest, demand, influence, award, deployment or endorsement.
Corporations Canada discloses only one 25% to 50% significant-control interest; the remaining cap table and full Canadian ownership are unresolved.
The speech-translation record is a published patent application family and the ANVIL mark is advertised for opposition; neither supports a granted-patent or registered-trademark claim.
No public source resolved product accreditation, classification approval, Controlled Goods status, exact security-control mapping or mission-data residency.

The privacy policy's U.S. processing statement concerns covered personal information and must not be converted into a claim about classified or mission-data hosting.
The planned Project Convergence evaluation has no recovered public completion report, configuration, measured result or adoption decision.
The Cameroon vendor-country value in one Open Government contract row conflicts with ANVIL's Canadian corporate identity and Ottawa address and is excluded as a disclosure anomaly.
Current headcount is unresolved: dated federal supplier records and company-reported 2026 figures are not an independently audited workforce count.
